headline: Bangladesh to impose 15% tax on gold sales profits
summary: The government proposes a new tax on capital gains from the sale of gold and jewellery declared in income tax returns for the 2026-27 fiscal year.
details: The government is set to introduce a 15 percent tax on profits earned from the sale of gold or gold ornaments declared by individual taxpayers in their income tax returns.
This proposal is part of the amendments to the Income Tax Act for the 2026-27 fiscal year budget.

Under the new rule, income from gold sales will be treated as capital gains. The tax will be calculated based on the difference between the market value at the time of acquisition and the current market price.
National Board of Revenue (NBR) officials state that many taxpayers declare large gold holdings, often citing marriage gifts or inheritance, to later explain undisclosed income sources.
The NBR believes the quantity of gold shown in tax returns often exceeds the estimated stock of gold in the country, leading to this measure to curb tax evasion.
If a taxpayer fails to specify the acquisition value or timing of their gold, the entire value of the gold will be treated as capital gain and taxed at 15 percent.

headline_marked: [[JU student’s body recovered]] from Buriganga river in Dhaka
headline: JU student’s body recovered from Buriganga river in Dhaka
summary: Dip Mozumder, a 4th-year Biochemistry and Molecular Biology student, was found decomposed in the Bosila area after being missing since Friday.
details: The body of Dip Mozumder, a student of Jahangirnagar University (JU), was recovered from the Buriganga river in Dhaka's Bosila area on Monday afternoon.
According to Mahfujur Rahman, additional superintendent of Dhaka River Police, the body was found in a decomposed state after locals alerted the police around 4:30 PM.
Police identified the deceased through a university ID card and an admit card found on the body.
The student's family members, contacted by police, confirmed that Dip had been missing since Friday.
Prof Ashraful Hasan, Chairman of the Biochemistry and Molecular Biology department at JU, stated that Dip was approximately 23 years old and in the second semester of his fourth year.
Quoting friends, the department chairman added that Dip had allegedly left his home after a quarrel with his family.
The body has been sent to Sir Salimullah Medical College morgue for an autopsy to determine the cause of death.
caption:
A missing Jahangirnagar University student has been found dead in the Buriganga river.

The body of Dip Mozumder, a student of Jahangirnagar University (JU), was recovered from the Buriganga river in Dhaka's Bosila area on Monday afternoon.

According to Mahfujur Rahman, additional superintendent of Dhaka River Police, the body was found in a decomposed state after locals alerted the police around 4:30 PM.

Police identified the deceased through a university ID card and an admit card found on the body.

The student's family members, contacted by police, confirmed that Dip had been missing since Friday.

Prof Ashraful Hasan, Chairman of the Biochemistry and Molecular Biology department at JU, stated that Dip was approximately 23 years old and in the second semester of his fourth year.

Quoting friends, the department chairman added that Dip had allegedly left his home after a quarrel with his family.

The body has been sent to Sir Salimullah Medical College morgue for an autopsy to determine the cause of death.
